Week in brief

Entra week of 19 May: Private Access forward-proxy routing is recorded; new External ID/PIM guidance and two explicitly Preview security topics stand out

This was overwhelmingly a Microsoft Learn documentation period: 2,268 updates, five new records, and nine removals out of 2,282 changes, with no Message Center items. Most entries are page maintenance or clarification rather than product announcements. The meaningful exceptions are the Private Access connector's forward-proxy routing note, new External ID emailOtpSend and ID Governance/PIM for Groups procedures, and refreshed descriptions of TLS inspection and linkable identifiers. No supplied evidence establishes general availability, a retirement, or a tenant-wide rollout; the nine removals should not be read as product retirements.

  • Private Access · General
    Private Access: forward-proxy routing appears in connector version history

    The updated Version History says the connector now supports routing outbound traffic to destinations in Microsoft Entra Private Access through a forward proxy, describing this as improved network control. This is a concrete changed-behavior note in the documentation, but no connector version, prerequisites, availability label, or rollout timing is supplied. It gives forward-proxy deployments a specific routing capability to validate; it does not establish a tenant-wide change.

  • Internet Access · Authentication
    Global Secure Access and Internet Access: TLS inspection documentation is explicitly Preview

    The supplied records show updates to the TLS inspection page in Global Secure Access on 22 and 23 May and in Internet Access on 24 May. The pages describe terminating TLS at edge locations, decrypting and inspecting encrypted traffic, and applying controls such as threat detection, content filtering, and fine-grained access policies. The Preview label is explicit; these entries clarify the capability's documented scope rather than announce general availability or a rollout.

  • External ID · Authentication
    External ID: new emailOtpSend reference for custom authentication extensions

    The 20 May New page documents a custom authentication extension that invokes the emailOtpSend event in External ID customer configurations and retrieves and returns event data. Related updates cover the email OTP send event, custom authentication extensions, and adding MFA to customer applications. This is newly published integration guidance, not evidence that a new feature or GA milestone occurred this week; teams implementing custom email OTP handling have a more focused event reference to review.

  • ID Governance · Governance
    ID Governance: new PIM for Groups procedure for access packages

    The 23 May New how-to explains how to assign eligible group membership and ownership through PIM for Groups within an access package. An accompanying update says the setup includes creating the group that will be managed by PIM. This adds implementation guidance for an access-package and PIM scenario, but it does not establish a newly launched or generally available capability.

  • Entra ID · Authentication
    Entra ID security: linkable-identifiers Preview and Conditional Access coverage guidance

    An updated Entra ID article marked Preview describes using session IDs and unique token identifiers to track and investigate identity activities. Separately, the updated Plan Conditional Access guidance says every app should have at least one policy and favors a policy covering All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps'), so newly onboarded applications are included without repeatedly changing policy scope. The first is Preview capability documentation; the second is security guidance. Neither record reports an||||?

For Entra administrators

The feed does not identify an immediate tenant-wide action. The two highlighted New items are a reference page and a how-to, not launch or GA notices. Administrators with affected designs can review custom email OTP extensions, access packages using eligible PIM group membership or ownership, and Private Access topologies that use forward proxies. TLS inspection and linkable identifiers are explicitly Preview, so their entries should be read as evaluation and documentation context; the supplied summaries provide no rollout, prerequisite, or enablement instruction. The Conditional Access update is security guidance to cover every app—favoring All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')—not a report that tenant policies changed.

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.

23 May 2025

Manage Stale Devices

Updated

Because a stale device is defined as a registered device that hasn't been used to access any cloud apps for a specific timeframe, detecting stale devices requires a timestamp-related property. In Microsoft Entra ID, this property is called **ApproximateLastSignInDateTime** or **activity timestamp**. If the delta between now and the value of the **activity timestamp** exceeds the timeframe you've defined for active devices, a device is considered to be stale.

Application Management Certs Faq

Updated

By default, Microsoft Entra ID configures a certificate to expire after three years after being created automatically during SAML single sign-on configuration. Because you can't change the date of a certificate after you save it, you need to create a new certificate. For steps on how to do so, refer [Customize the expiration date for your federation certificate and roll it over to a new certificate](./tutorial-manage-certificates-for-federated-single-sign-on.md#customize-the-expiration-date-for-your-federation-certificate-and-roll-it-over-to-a-new-certificate).

Emergency Access Accounts

Updated

Microsoft recommends that organizations have two cloud-only emergency access accounts permanently assigned the [Global Administrator](/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#global-administrator) role. These accounts are highly privileged and aren't assigned to specific individuals. The accounts are limited to emergency or "break glass" scenarios where normal accounts can't be used or all other administrators are accidentally locked out. These accounts should be created following the [emergency access account recommendations](/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access).

23 May 2025

Entitlement Management Access Package Auto Assignment Policy

Updated

You can use rules to determine access package assignment based on user properties in Microsoft Entra ID, part of Microsoft Entra. In Entitlement Management, an access package can have multiple policies, and each policy establishes how users get an assignment to the access package, and for how long. As an administrator, you can establish a policy for automatic assignments by supplying a membership rule, that Entitlement Management follows to create and remove assignments automatically. Similar to a [dynamic group](../identity/users/groups-create-rule.md), when an automatic assignment policy is created, user attributes are evaluated for matches with the policy's membership rule. When an attribute changes for a user, these automatic assignment policy rules in the access packages are processed for membership changes. Assignments to users are then added or removed depending on whether they meet the rule criteria.

When you add a guest user to your directory, the guest user account has a consent status (viewable in PowerShell) that’s initially set to **PendingAcceptance**. External Identities Overview

Updated

Azure Active Directory B2C (Azure AD B2C) is Microsoft's legacy solution for customer identity and access management. Azure AD B2C includes a separate consumer-based directory that you manage in the Azure portal through the Azure AD B2C service. Each Azure AD B2C tenant is separate and distinct from other Microsoft Entra ID and Azure AD B2C tenants. The Azure AD B2C portal experience is similar to Microsoft Entra ID, but there are key differences, such as the ability to customize your user journeys using the Identity Experience Framework.
